Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 43, verses 9–14:

Allah the Exalted says: And if you (O Muhammad) ask these polytheists, who worship others besides Him along with Allah, ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth?﴾ they will surely say, ﴿They were created by the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ That is, they will acknowledge that the Creator of those things is Allah [the Exalted] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] alone, with no partner, and yet along with this they worship others besides Him, such as idols and rivals.

Then He said: ﴿He who made the earth for you as a cradle﴾ That is, a resting place, a firm bed, on which you walk, stand, sleep, and move about, even though it was created upon the surge of water. But He anchored it with mountains so that it would not sway this way or that. ﴿And made for you therein roads﴾ That is, paths between the mountains and the valleys, ﴿that you may be guided.﴾ That is, in your travel from town to town, from region to region, and from climate to climate.

﴿And who sends down water from the sky in measure﴾ That is, in the amount sufficient for your crops, your fruits, and your drinking, for yourselves and your livestock. ﴿Then We revive thereby a dead land﴾ That is, a land that was dead. When the water reaches it, it stirs and swells and grows every lovely kind of plant. He then drew attention, through the reviving of the earth, to the reviving of bodies on the Day of Return after their death, and said: ﴿Thus you will be brought forth.﴾

Then He said: ﴿And who created all the kinds [of things] in pairs﴾ That is, among what the earth produces of all types: plants, crops, fruits, and flowers, and other things, [that is] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] among the animals of their various species and kinds. ﴿And made for you ships and livestock to ride﴾ That is, the boats and the cattle. He made them subservient to you, subjected them, and made them easy for you, so that you may eat their meat, drink their milk, and ride on their backs. For this reason He said: ﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs﴾ That is, so that you may settle comfortably and securely ﴿upon their backs,﴾ that is, upon the backs of this kind of animal. ﴿Then remember the favor of your Lord﴾ That is, concerning what He has subjected for you, ﴿when you are settled upon them, and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have controlled it [ourselves]."﴾ That is, we could not have overpowered it. Had Allah not subjected this to us, we would not have been able to control it.

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Could not have controlled it﴾ means could not have been capable of it.

﴿And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.﴾ That is, we will surely go back to Him after our death, and toward Him is our greatest journey. This is a form of drawing attention, through the journey of this world, to the journey of the Hereafter, just as He drew attention, through worldly provision, to the provision of the Hereafter in His saying: ﴿And take provision, but the best provision is piety﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 197], and through worldly clothing, to the clothing of the Hereafter in His saying: ﴿And [as] adornment; but the garment of righteousness—that is best. That is among the signs of Allah﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26].

Mention of the hadiths related to mounting a riding animal:

The hadith of the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him:

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Shurayk ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah, who said: I saw 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, being brought a riding animal. When he placed his foot in the stirrup, he said: "In the name of Allah." When he settled upon it, he said: "All praise is for Allah," and then: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have controlled it [ourselves]. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.﴾ Then he praised Allah three times, glorified Him three times, and then said: "Glory be to You, there is no god but You; I have wronged myself, so forgive me." Then he laughed. I said to him: "What made you laugh, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do as I did, and then he laughed. I said: 'What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The Lord is amazed at His servant when he says: My Lord, forgive me. And He says: My servant knows that none forgives sins except Me.'"

Thus it was related by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas (al-Nasa'i added: and Mansur), from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Asadi al-Walibi, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (1/97), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2602), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3446), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (8800).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said, on the authority of Shu'bah: I said to Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i: "From whom did you hear this hadith?" He said: "From Yunus ibn Khabbab." So I met Yunus ibn Khabbab and said: "From whom did you hear it?" He said: "From a man who heard it from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah." It was also related by some narrators from Yunus ibn Khabbab, from Shaqiq ibn 'Uqbah al-Asadi, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Walibi, with the same wording. [[Tuhfat al-Ashraf by al-Mizzi (7/436).]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them:

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had him ride behind him on his mount. When he settled upon it, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said "Allahu Akbar" three times, praised Allah three times, and declared "La ilaha illa Allah" once. Then he leaned back on it and laughed. Then he turned to him and said: "There is no Muslim man who mounts a riding animal and does as I have done, except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, turns to him, and laughs toward him as I have laughed toward you." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/330). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/131): "It contains Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak."]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them:

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bariqi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he mounted his riding camel, would say "Allahu Akbar" three times, and then recite: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have controlled it [ourselves]. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.﴾ Then he would say: "O Allah, I ask You on this journey of mine for righteousness and piety, and for deeds that please You. O Allah, make this journey easy for us and fold up its distance for us. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor over the family. O Allah, accompany us on our journey and be our successor over our family." And when he returned to his family he would say: "We are returning, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord, if Allah wills."

Thus it was related by Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, and by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, both of them from Abu al-Zubayr, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (2/144), Sahih Muslim no. (1342), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2599), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (10382), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3447).]]

Another hadith:

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from 'Amr ibn al-Hakam ibn Thawban, [[In manuscript T: "Imam Ahmad related it with his chain."]] from Abu Las al-Khuza'i, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) carried us on camels from the camels of charity to the Hajj. We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we do not think these should carry us!" He said: "There is not a camel but that on its hump there is a devil. So mention the name of Allah over them when you mount them, as I command you, and then treat them gently for your own benefit, for it is only Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who carries [them]." [[Al-Musnad (4/221), and its narrators are trustworthy.]]

Abu Las's name is Muhammad ibn al-Aswad ibn Khalaf.

Another hadith with the same meaning:

Ahmad said: Attab narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us (ḥ), and 'Ali ibn Ishaq informed us, 'Abd Allah (meaning Ibn al-Mubarak) informed us, Usamah ibn Zayd informed us, Muhammad ibn Hamzah informed me, that he heard his father say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "On the back of every camel is a devil. So if you ride them, mention the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and then do not fall short of your needs." [[Al-Musnad (3/494). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/131): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Muhammad ibn Hamzah, who is trustworthy."]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 43, verses 9–14:

Allah the Exalted says: And if you (O Muhammad) ask these polytheists, who worship others besides Him along with Allah, ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth?﴾ they will surely say, ﴿They were created by the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ That is, they will acknowledge that the Creator of those things is Allah [the Exalted] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] alone, with no partner, and yet along with this they worship others besides Him, such as idols and rivals.

Then He said: ﴿He who made the earth for you as a cradle﴾ That is, a resting place, a firm bed, on which you walk, stand, sleep, and move about, even though it was created upon the surge of water. But He anchored it with mountains so that it would not sway this way or that. ﴿And made for you therein roads﴾ That is, paths between the mountains and the valleys, ﴿that you may be guided.﴾ That is, in your travel from town to town, from region to region, and from climate to climate.

﴿And who sends down water from the sky in measure﴾ That is, in the amount sufficient for your crops, your fruits, and your drinking, for yourselves and your livestock. ﴿Then We revive thereby a dead land﴾ That is, a land that was dead. When the water reaches it, it stirs and swells and grows every lovely kind of plant. He then drew attention, through the reviving of the earth, to the reviving of bodies on the Day of Return after their death, and said: ﴿Thus you will be brought forth.﴾

Then He said: ﴿And who created all the kinds [of things] in pairs﴾ That is, among what the earth produces of all types: plants, crops, fruits, and flowers, and other things, [that is] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] among the animals of their various species and kinds. ﴿And made for you ships and livestock to ride﴾ That is, the boats and the cattle. He made them subservient to you, subjected them, and made them easy for you, so that you may eat their meat, drink their milk, and ride on their backs. For this reason He said: ﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs﴾ That is, so that you may settle comfortably and securely ﴿upon their backs,﴾ that is, upon the backs of this kind of animal. ﴿Then remember the favor of your Lord﴾ That is, concerning what He has subjected for you, ﴿when you are settled upon them, and say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have controlled it [ourselves]."﴾ That is, we could not have overpowered it. Had Allah not subjected this to us, we would not have been able to control it.

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Could not have controlled it﴾ means could not have been capable of it.

﴿And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.﴾ That is, we will surely go back to Him after our death, and toward Him is our greatest journey. This is a form of drawing attention, through the journey of this world, to the journey of the Hereafter, just as He drew attention, through worldly provision, to the provision of the Hereafter in His saying: ﴿And take provision, but the best provision is piety﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 197], and through worldly clothing, to the clothing of the Hereafter in His saying: ﴿And [as] adornment; but the garment of righteousness—that is best. That is among the signs of Allah﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26].

Mention of the hadiths related to mounting a riding animal:

The hadith of the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him:

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Shurayk ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah, who said: I saw 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, being brought a riding animal. When he placed his foot in the stirrup, he said: "In the name of Allah." When he settled upon it, he said: "All praise is for Allah," and then: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have controlled it [ourselves]. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return.﴾ Then he praised Allah three times, glorified Him three times, and then said: "Glory be to You, there is no god but You; I have wronged myself, so forgive me." Then he laughed. I said to him: "What made you laugh, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do as I did, and then he laughed. I said: 'What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The Lord is amazed at His servant when he says: My Lord, forgive me. And He says: My servant knows that none forgives sins except Me.'"

Thus it was related by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas (al-Nasa'i added: and Mansur), from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Asadi al-Walibi, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (1/97), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2602), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3446), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (8800).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said, on the authority of Shu'bah: I said to Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i: "From whom did you hear this hadith?" He said: "From Yunus ibn Khabbab." So I met Yunus ibn Khabbab and said: "From whom did you hear it?" He said: "From a man who heard it from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah." It was also related by some narrators from Yunus ibn Khabbab, from Shaqiq ibn 'Uqbah al-Asadi, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Walibi, with the same wording. [[Tuhfat al-Ashraf by al-Mizzi (7/436).]]

The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them:

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had him ride behind him on his mount. When he settled upon it, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said "Allahu Akbar" three times, praised Allah three times, and declared "La ilaha illa Allah" once. Then he leaned back on it and laughed. Then he turned to him and said: "There is no Muslim man who mounts a riding animal and does as I have done, except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, turns to him, and laughs toward him as I have laughed toward you." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/330). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/131): "It contains Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak."]]

The Most High says, reporting about the polytheists in what they invented and lied about, in their division of some livestock for their idols (ṭawāghīt) and some for God, as God mentioned about them in Surat al-An'am, in His words: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the tilth and livestock, and they say, "This is for God," by their claim, and "This is for our partners." So what is for their partners does not reach God, but what is for God reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge.﴾ [al-An'am: 136]. Likewise, they assigned to Him from both kinds, the daughters and the sons, the lesser and more base of the two, which is the daughters, as the Most High said: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That would be an unjust division!﴾ [al-Najm: 21–22]. Here He said: ﴿And they have assigned to Him from His servants a portion. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ This is an utmost denunciation of them. Then He mentioned the completion of the denunciation, saying: ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.﴾ That is, when one of these people is given news of what they attribute to God, of daughters, he is extremely disdainful of it, and sorrow overwhelms him at the evil of what he was given news of, and he hides from the people out of shame for it. The Most High says: How, then, do you disdain it, while you attribute it to God, Mighty and Majestic?

Then He said: ﴿Is one who is brought up in ornament and is in disputation unclear?﴾ That is, the woman is deficient, and her deficiency is completed by wearing ornaments from the time she is a little girl. When she argues, she has no expression; rather, she is incapable and inarticulate. Shall one who is like this be attributed to the majesty of God, Mighty and Majestic?! So the female is deficient in outward and inward nature, in form and in meaning. Thus the deficiency of her outward appearance and form is completed by wearing ornaments and what is similar to them, so that what is lacking in her may be compensated. As one of the Arab poets said:

"Ornament is only a remedy for a deficiency... it completes beauty when beauty falls short.
And as for one whose beauty is abundant... like your beauty, he has no need to be adorned."

As for the deficiency of her meaning, she is weak and incapable of defending herself when it is time to defend, having neither expression nor resolve. As one of the Arabs said when he was given news of a daughter: "She is not a fine child: her support is weeping, and her kindness is theft."

God, exalted is He, says, reporting about His servant, messenger, and close friend, Ibrahim (Abraham), the leader of the hunafa' (monotheists), and the father of all the prophets sent after him, the one whom Quraysh trace their lineage and religion to: that he disowned his father and his people for their worship of idols. So he said: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except for He who created me, for indeed He will guide me.﴾ And ﴿He made it a word that remains among his descendants﴾, meaning this word, which is the worship of God alone, without partner, and the rejection of everything other than Him among the idols, and it is "There is no god but God." That is, He made it lasting among his offspring, so that whoever Allah guided from the descendants of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, would follow him in it, ﴿that they may return﴾, that is, to it.

ʿIkrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others [[In T: "and others"]] said, regarding His saying ﴿and He made it a word that remains among his descendants﴾: it means "There is no god but God"; there will always be among his descendants someone who says it. A similar report is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Ibn Zayd said: it is the word of Islam. This goes back to what the majority said.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, I gave enjoyment to these [people]﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿and their fathers﴾, that is, their life was prolonged for them in their misguidance, ﴿until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger﴾, that is, one clear in his message and warning.

﴿And when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾ That is, they stubbornly opposed it, rejected it, and pushed it away with their chests and palms out of disbelief, envy, and insolence. ﴿And they said﴾ [meaning] [[Added from T and M.]] as objectors to Him who sent it down, the Exalted and Most Holy: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two towns?﴾ That is: why was this Qur'an not sent down to a man great and important in their eyes from the two towns? They meant Makkah and al-Ta'if. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrimah, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd.

Several scholars [[In M and A: "among them and Qatadah"]] have mentioned that they meant by this al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and ʿUrwah ibn Masʿud al-Thaqafi.

Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi: they meant al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and Masʿud ibn ʿAmr al-Thaqafi.

From Mujahid: ʿUmayr ibn ʿAmr ibn Masʿud al-Thaqafi. And also from him: they meant al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and Habib ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr al-Thaqafi.

From Mujahid: they meant ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah in Makkah, and Ibn ʿAbd Yalil in al-Ta'if.

al-Suddi said: they meant [by this] [[Added from A.]] al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and Kinanah ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr al-Thaqafi.

The apparent meaning is that they meant a great man from whichever of the two towns he was.

God, exalted, said, refuting them in this objection: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾ That is: the matter is not referred to them, but to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah knows best where to place His messages, for He sends them down only upon the purest of creation in heart and soul, and the most noble of them in lineage and the most pure in origin.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Ask them on the night of the Night Journey (al-Isra'), for the prophets were gathered for him." Ibn Jarir chose the first view, [and Allah knows best] [[Addition from manuscript A.]].

The Most High says, reporting about Pharaoh, his rebellion, his arrogance, his disbelief and his obstinacy: he gathered his people and called out to them, boasting and priding himself on the kingdom of Egypt and his control over it: ﴿Does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ Qatadah said: "They had gardens and streams of water." ﴿Do you not see?﴾ That is, do you not see the greatness and kingship I possess, meaning, and Musa and his followers[^1] are poor and weak? This is like His saying: ﴿So he gathered [his people] and called out, saying, "I am your lord, the most high." So Allah seized him in the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 23–25].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or am I better than this one who is contemptible?﴾ Al-Suddi said: "He is saying, 'Rather, I am better than this one who is contemptible.'" Likewise some of the grammarians of Basra said that *ʾam* (أم) here means *bal* (بل, "rather"). What supports this is what al-Farra' reported from some of the readers, that he recited it as: "*Amā* anā khayrun min hādhā alladhī huwa mahīn" (أمَا أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ). Ibn Jarir said: "Even if this reading were authentic, its meaning would be sound and clear, but it contradicts the reading of the major cities, for they read: ﴿Am anā khayrun min hādhā alladhī huwa mahīn?﴾ (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ) as a question."

I say: In any case, what Pharaoh—may the curse of Allah be upon him—means is that he is better than Musa, peace be upon him. In this statement he lied, an obvious and clear lie, so upon him be the continuous curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

By His saying ﴿contemptible﴾ (مَهِينٌ) he meant, as Sufyan said: "despicable." Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "That is, weak." Ibn Jarir said: "That is, he has no kingdom, no authority, and no wealth."

﴿And he can hardly express himself clearly﴾ (وَلا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ): that is, he can hardly speak clearly, so he is tongue-tied and unable to speak fluently.

Al-Suddi said: "﴿He can hardly express himself clearly﴾ means he can hardly make himself understood." Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir said: "That is, a stammer of the tongue." Sufyan said: "That is, there was something wrong with his tongue from the ember when he placed it in his mouth as a child."

What Pharaoh—may Allah curse him—said is a lie and a fabrication. What drove him to this was disbelief and obstinacy, as he looked at Musa, peace be upon him, with a disbelieving and wretched eye. Musa, peace be upon him, possessed such majesty, grandeur and splendour in appearance that it dazzles the sight of those with understanding. His saying ﴿contemptible﴾ is a lie; rather, he is contemptible, lowly in form, character and religion. Musa [peace be upon him] was noble, a leader, truthful, righteous and rightly guided. His saying ﴿and he can hardly express himself clearly﴾ is also a fabrication. Although something of that ember did affect his tongue in childhood, he asked Allah, mighty and majestic, to loosen a knot from his tongue so that they would understand his speech, and Allah answered him in His saying: ﴿He said, "You have been granted your request, O Musa."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 36]. Even if something remained that he did not ask to be removed, as al-Hasan al-Basri said, what he asked to remove was what prevents conveying and understanding. Physical features that are not of a person's own doing are not blamed or reproached. Pharaoh, although he understood and had reason, knew this, but he wanted to deceive his subjects, for they were ignorant and dull.

Likewise is His saying: ﴿Why then has he not been bestowed bracelets of gold?﴾ That is, *asawira* (أَسَاوِرَةٌ), which are ornaments placed on the wrists, as Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others said. ﴿Or accompanied by angels in procession?﴾ That is, surrounding him in service and bearing witness to his truthfulness. He looked at the outward appearance and did not grasp the inner, spiritual reality, which, had he known, was more evident than what he looked at. Therefore Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿So he deceived his people, and they obeyed him.﴾ That is, he made their minds foolish; he called them to error and they responded to him. ﴿Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾

Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.﴾ Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "﴿Angered Us﴾ (آسَفُونَا) means made Us wrathful."

Al-Dahhak reported from him: "Made Us angry." Ibn Abbas also said this, as did Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others among the commentators.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubaydullah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us: my uncle narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Uqbah ibn Muslim al-Tujibi, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see Allah, mighty and majestic, giving a servant whatever he wishes while he persists in his sins, that is only a gradual leading toward ruin from Him." Then he recited: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them.﴾[^2]

And my father narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: "I was with Abdullah when sudden death was mentioned in his presence. He said: 'It is a relief for the believer and a regret for the disbeliever.' Then he recited: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them.﴾"

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I found retribution to be with heedlessness," meaning His saying: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We made them a precedent and an example for the later generations.﴾ Abu Mijlaz said: "﴿A precedent﴾ (سَلَفًا) for the like of those who act as they did."

He and Mujahid said: "﴿And an example﴾ (وَمَثَلًا), that is, a lesson for those after them."

[^1]: In manuscript A: "and those with him."
[^2]: Al-Tabarani reported it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4926) "Majma' al-Bahrayn," and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (4540), via the chain of Abdullah ibn Salih from Harmalah ibn Imran with the same wording. Ahmad reported it in his Musnad (4/145) from Rashdin ibn Sa'd, and al-Dulabi in al-Kuna (1/111) from Hajjaj ibn Sulayman, both from Harmalah ibn Imran with the same wording. Al-Hafiz al-Iraqi graded it hasan in his takhrij of the hadiths of Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din.

Ibn Jarir said: "Even if this reading were authentic, its meaning would be sound and clear, but it contradicts the reading of the major cities, for they read: ﴿Am anā khayrun min hādhā alladhī huwa mahīn?﴾ (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هَذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ) as a question."

I say: In any case, what Pharaoh—may the curse of Allah be upon him—means is that he is better than Musa, peace be upon him. In this statement he lied, an obvious and clear lie, so upon him be the continuous curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

By His saying ﴿contemptible﴾ (مَهِينٌ) he meant, as Sufyan said: "despicable." Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "That is, weak." Ibn Jarir said: "That is, he has no kingdom, no authority, and no wealth."

﴿And he can hardly express himself clearly﴾ (وَلا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ): that is, he can hardly speak clearly, so he is tongue-tied and unable to speak fluently.

Al-Suddi said: "﴿He can hardly express himself clearly﴾ means he can hardly make himself understood." Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir said: "That is, a stammer of the tongue." Sufyan said: "That is, there was something wrong with his tongue from the ember when he placed it in his mouth as a child."

What Pharaoh—may Allah curse him—said is a lie and a fabrication. What drove him to this was disbelief and obstinacy, as he looked at Musa, peace be upon him, with a disbelieving and wretched eye. Musa, peace be upon him, possessed such majesty, grandeur and splendour in appearance that it dazzles the sight of those with understanding. His saying ﴿contemptible﴾ is a lie; rather, he is contemptible, lowly in form, character and religion. Musa [peace be upon him] was noble, a leader, truthful, righteous and rightly guided. His saying ﴿and he can hardly express himself clearly﴾ is also a fabrication. Although something of that ember did affect his tongue in childhood, he asked Allah, mighty and majestic, to loosen a knot from his tongue so that they would understand his speech, and Allah answered him in His saying: ﴿He said, "You have been granted your request, O Musa."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 36]. Even if something remained that he did not ask to be removed, as al-Hasan al-Basri said, what he asked to remove was what prevents conveying and understanding. Physical features that are not of a person's own doing are not blamed or reproached. Pharaoh, although he understood and had reason, knew this, but he wanted to deceive his subjects, for they were ignorant and dull.

Likewise is His saying: ﴿Why then has he not been bestowed bracelets of gold?﴾ That is, *asawira* (أَسَاوِرَةٌ), which are ornaments placed on the wrists, as Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others said. ﴿Or accompanied by angels in procession?﴾ That is, surrounding him in service and bearing witness to his truthfulness. He looked at the outward appearance and did not grasp the inner, spiritual reality, which, had he known, was more evident than what he looked at. Therefore Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿So he deceived his people, and they obeyed him.﴾ That is, he made their minds foolish; he called them to error and they responded to him. ﴿Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾

Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.﴾ Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: "﴿Angered Us﴾ (آسَفُونَا) means made Us wrathful."

Al-Dahhak reported from him: "Made Us angry." Ibn Abbas also said this, as did Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others among the commentators.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubaydullah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us: my uncle narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Uqbah ibn Muslim al-Tujibi, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see Allah, mighty and majestic, giving a servant whatever he wishes while he persists in his sins, that is only a gradual leading toward ruin from Him." Then he recited: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them.﴾[^2]

And my father narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: "I was with Abdullah when sudden death was mentioned in his presence. He said: 'It is a relief for the believer and a regret for the disbeliever.' Then he recited: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them.﴾"

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I found retribution to be with heedlessness," meaning His saying: ﴿And when they angered Us, We took retribution from them and drowned them all.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We made them a precedent and an example for the later generations.﴾ Abu Mijlaz said: "﴿A precedent﴾ (سَلَفًا) for the like of those who act as they did."

He and Mujahid said: "﴿And an example﴾ (وَمَثَلًا), that is, a lesson for those after them."

[^1]: In manuscript A: "and those with him."
[^2]: Al-Tabarani reported it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4926) "Majma' al-Bahrayn," and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (4540), via the chain of Abdullah ibn Salih from Harmalah ibn Imran with the same wording. Ahmad reported it in his Musnad (4/145) from Rashdin ibn Sa'd, and al-Dulabi in al-Kuna (1/111) from Hajjaj ibn Sulayman, both from Harmalah ibn Imran with the same wording. Al-Hafiz al-Iraqi graded it hasan in his takhrij of the hadiths of Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾ أَيْ: لَا تَشُكُّوا [[في ت، م، أ: "تشكون".]] فِيهَا، إِنَّهَا وَاقِعَةٌ وَكَائِنَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ، ﴿وَاتَّبَعُونِ﴾ أَيْ: فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِ ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ أَيْ: عَنِ اتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ عِيسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالنُّبُوَّةِ ﴿وَلأبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: يَعْنِي مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ لَا الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ [[تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) .]]. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ حَسَنٌ جَيِّدٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ قَوْلَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ "بَعْضَ" هَاهُنَا بمعنى "كل"، واستشهد بقول لبيد الشاعر: تَرّاك أمْكنَة إذَا لَمْ أرْضَها [[في أ: "أرمنها".]] أَوْ يَعْتَلق [[في أ: "يقتلوا".]] بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حمَامُها [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) وديوان لبيد العامري (ص٣١٣) .]]

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾ أَيْ: لَا تَشُكُّوا [[في ت، م، أ: "تشكون".]] فِيهَا، إِنَّهَا وَاقِعَةٌ وَكَائِنَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ، ﴿وَاتَّبَعُونِ﴾ أَيْ: فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِ ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ أَيْ: عَنِ اتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ عِيسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالنُّبُوَّةِ ﴿وَلأبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: يَعْنِي مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ لَا الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ [[تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) .]]. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ حَسَنٌ جَيِّدٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ قَوْلَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ "بَعْضَ" هَاهُنَا بمعنى "كل"، واستشهد بقول لبيد الشاعر: تَرّاك أمْكنَة إذَا لَمْ أرْضَها [[في أ: "أرمنها".]] أَوْ يَعْتَلق [[في أ: "يقتلوا".]] بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حمَامُها [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) وديوان لبيد العامري (ص٣١٣) .]]

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'"
