(48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾ أَيْ: لَا تَشُكُّوا [[في ت، م، أ: "تشكون".]] فِيهَا، إِنَّهَا وَاقِعَةٌ وَكَائِنَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ، ﴿وَاتَّبَعُونِ﴾ أَيْ: فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِ ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ أَيْ: عَنِ اتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ عِيسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالنُّبُوَّةِ ﴿وَلأبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: يَعْنِي مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ لَا الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ [[تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) .]]. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ حَسَنٌ جَيِّدٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ قَوْلَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ "بَعْضَ" هَاهُنَا بمعنى "كل"، واستشهد بقول لبيد الشاعر: تَرّاك أمْكنَة إذَا لَمْ أرْضَها [[في أ: "أرمنها".]] أَوْ يَعْتَلق [[في أ: "يقتلوا".]] بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حمَامُها [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) وديوان لبيد العامري (ص٣١٣) .]]

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

[[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾ أَيْ: لَا تَشُكُّوا [[في ت، م، أ: "تشكون".]] فِيهَا، إِنَّهَا وَاقِعَةٌ وَكَائِنَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ، ﴿وَاتَّبَعُونِ﴾ أَيْ: فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِ ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ أَيْ: عَنِ اتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ عِيسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالنُّبُوَّةِ ﴿وَلأبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: يَعْنِي مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ لَا الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ [[تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) .]]. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ حَسَنٌ جَيِّدٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ قَوْلَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ "بَعْضَ" هَاهُنَا بمعنى "كل"، واستشهد بقول لبيد الشاعر: تَرّاك أمْكنَة إذَا لَمْ أرْضَها [[في أ: "أرمنها".]] أَوْ يَعْتَلق [[في أ: "يقتلوا".]] بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حمَامُها [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) وديوان لبيد العامري (ص٣١٣) .]]

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾ أَيْ: لَا تَشُكُّوا [[في ت، م، أ: "تشكون".]] فِيهَا، إِنَّهَا وَاقِعَةٌ وَكَائِنَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ، ﴿وَاتَّبَعُونِ﴾ أَيْ: فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِ ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ أَيْ: عَنِ اتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ عِيسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالنُّبُوَّةِ ﴿وَلأبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: يَعْنِي مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ لَا الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ [[تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) .]]. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ حَسَنٌ جَيِّدٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ قَوْلَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ "بَعْضَ" هَاهُنَا بمعنى "كل"، واستشهد بقول لبيد الشاعر: تَرّاك أمْكنَة إذَا لَمْ أرْضَها [[في أ: "أرمنها".]] أَوْ يَعْتَلق [[في أ: "يقتلوا".]] بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حمَامُها [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) وديوان لبيد العامري (ص٣١٣) .]]

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِهَا﴾ أَيْ: لَا تَشُكُّوا [[في ت، م، أ: "تشكون".]] فِيهَا، إِنَّهَا وَاقِعَةٌ وَكَائِنَةٌ لَا مَحَالَةَ، ﴿وَاتَّبَعُونِ﴾ أَيْ: فِيمَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِهِ ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ أَيْ: عَنِ اتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ ﴿إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ عِيسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالنُّبُوَّةِ ﴿وَلأبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾

قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: يَعْنِي مِنَ الْأُمُورِ الدِّينِيَّةِ لَا الدُّنْيَوِيَّةِ [[تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) .]]. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ حَسَنٌ جَيِّدٌ، ثُمَّ رَدَّ قَوْلَ مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ "بَعْضَ" هَاهُنَا بمعنى "كل"، واستشهد بقول لبيد الشاعر: تَرّاك أمْكنَة إذَا لَمْ أرْضَها [[في أ: "أرمنها".]] أَوْ يَعْتَلق [[في أ: "يقتلوا".]] بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حمَامُها [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (٢٥/٥٥) وديوان لبيد العامري (ص٣١٣) .]]

وَأَوَّلُوهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرَادَ جَمِيعَ النُّفُوسِ. قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: وَإِنَّمَا أَرَادَ نَفْسَهُ فَقَطْ، وَعَبَّرَ بِالْبَعْضِ عَنْهَا. وَهَذَا الَّذِي قَالَهُ مُحْتَمَلٌ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَيْ: [فِيمَا] [[زيادة من ت، م، أ.]] أَمَرَكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾، فِيمَا جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ، ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: أَنَا وَأَنْتُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، فُقَرَاءُ إِلَيْهِ، مُشْتَرِكُونَ فِي عِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، ﴿هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: هَذَا الَّذِي جِئْتُكُمْ بِهِ هُوَ الصِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ، وَهُوَ عِبَادَةُ الرَّبِّ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَحْدَهُ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزَابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ﴾ أَيِ: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْفِرَقُ وَصَارُوا شِيَعًا فِيهِ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُقِرُّ بِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ -وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ- وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ اللَّهِ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إِنَّهُ اللَّهُ -تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا- وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 57–65 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the obstinacy of the Quraysh in their disbelief and their deliberate stubbornness and disputation: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it [in mockery]﴾. Many scholars said, from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi: "yasuddun" means "yadhakun" (they laugh), i.e., they were amazed by it. [[In T and A: "And 'Ikrimah and others said: that is, they marvel."]]

Qatadah said: they become distressed and laugh. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: they turn away.

The reason for this is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the Sirah (Life of the Prophet), where he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, sat one day with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the Mosque. Then al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the gathering were several men of the Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith confronted him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ debated with him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], and the verses that follow. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara al-Tamimi [in T, M, A: "al-Sahmi"] approached and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to him: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, nor did he sit down. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of our gods are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have argued against him. Ask Muhammad: Is everything that is worshipped besides Allah in Hell along with those who worshipped it? We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship the Messiah [Isa], the son of Mary?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the gathering were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara, and they saw that he had argued and disputed. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him, for they only worship Satan and whoever commanded them to worship him." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us - those will be kept far away from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 101], meaning 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped along with them from the rabbis and monks who had died in obedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, whom those in misguidance who worshipped them took as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26], and the verses. And it was revealed concerning what is mentioned about the matter of 'Isa, that he is worshipped besides Allah. The amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, meaning: they turn away from your command by this statement of yours. Then he mentioned 'Isa, saying: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels replacing you upon the earth. And indeed, he [i.e., 'Isa] is a sign [knowledge] for the Hour﴾, meaning: the signs We placed at his hands, such as raising the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the knowledge of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful of it, but follow Me. This is a straight path﴾ [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358).]].

Ibn Jarir reported, through al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾, he said: it refers to the Quraysh, when it was said to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98], to the end of the verses. The Quraysh said to him: "Then what about the son of Mary?" He said: "That is the servant of Allah and His Messenger." They said: "By Allah, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, just as the Christians took 'Isa, the son of Mary, as a lord." Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave of Ibn 'Uqayl al-Ansari, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I know a verse of the Quran that no man has ever asked me about. I do not know whether people knew it and therefore did not ask about it, or did not notice it so as to ask about it." He said: Then he began to speak to us, and when he stood up we blamed ourselves that we had not asked him about it. So I said: "I will ask him when he comes tomorrow." When tomorrow came, I said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, yesterday you mentioned that a verse of the Quran no man had ever asked you about, and you do not know whether people knew it or did not notice it?" I said: "Tell me about it and about those that you recited before it." He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Quraysh: 'O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good.'" The Quraysh knew that the Christians worship 'Isa, the son of Mary, and what do they say about Muhammad? They said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? If you are truthful, then our gods are as you say." He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. I said: "What is 'yasuddun'?" He said: "They laugh." ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾. He said: "It is the coming forth of 'Isa, the son of Mary, before the Resurrection." [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Adam narrated to us, Shayban narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Ahmad, a freed slave of the Ansar [in A: "of the Ansariyyin"], from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, there is no one worshipped besides Allah in whom there is good." They said to him: "Do you not claim that 'Isa was a prophet and a righteous servant of the servants of Allah? Then he was worshipped besides Allah?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/154).]]

Mujahid said concerning His statement: ﴿And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it﴾: The Quraysh said: "Muhammad only wants us to worship him, just as the people of 'Isa worshipped 'Isa." Qatadah said something similar.

* *

His statement: ﴿And they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?"﴾. Qatadah said: they say: "Our gods are better than him." Qatadah also said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And they say, 'Are our gods better, or is this one?'" meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His statement: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument﴾, i.e., contention. And they knew that it does not apply to the verse, because it concerns what does not reason; and it is His statement: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya' 98]. Moreover, it is addressed to the Quraysh, and they were only worshipping idols and rivals, and they were not worshipping the Messiah so that they would bring him up. Thus it is established that their statement was only argument on their part; they did not believe in its soundness.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people went astray after guidance they were upon, except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited this verse: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾.

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Dinar, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/256), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3253), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (48), and Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih; we do not know it except from his hadith," so he said.

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu Umamah with an addition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Humayd ibn 'Ayyash al-Ramli narrated to us, Mu'mmal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ibn Makhzum informed us, from al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, from Abu Umamah. Hammad said: "I do not know whether he raised it [to the Prophet] or not." He said: "No nation went astray after its prophet except that the first of its misguidance was denying divine decree, and no nation went astray after its prophet except that they were given argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[In its chain is al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Shami, whom Ibn Hibban declared weak, saying: "He used to narrate from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mu'dilat (narrations with missing links)."]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim [in A: "Ja'far ibn al-Qasim"], from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to the people while they were disputing about the Quran, and he became extremely angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face. Then he said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah with one part against another, for no people ever went astray except that they were given [in T: "inherited"] argumentativeness," then he recited: ﴿They did not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/53).]]

* *

His statement: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him: he was nothing but a servant [from among the servants of Allah] upon whom Allah bestowed favor with prophethood and messengership. ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾, i.e., a proof, an argument and a demonstration of Our power over what We will.

* *

His statement: ﴿And if We willed, We could make from you﴾, i.e., instead of you, ﴿angels upon the earth replacing [you]﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They would replace you in it." Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Some of them would succeed others, just as some of you succeed others." This statement necessarily entails the first. Mujahid said: "They would populate the earth instead of you."

* *

His statement: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾: The explanation of Ibn Ishaq has preceded: that what is meant by this is what 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent with, of raising the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and other sicknesses. But there is consideration in this. Further from it is what Qatadah reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that the pronoun in ﴿And indeed, he﴾ refers to the Quran. Rather, the correct view is that it refers to 'Isa [peace be upon him] [[Addition from T.]], since the context is about him. Then what is meant by this is his descent before the Day of Resurrection, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that they will surely believe in him before his death﴾ [al-Nisa' 159], i.e., before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him, then ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 159]. This meaning is supported by the other reading: "wa-innahu la-'alam lil-sa'ah", i.e., a sign and proof of the occurrence of the Hour. Mujahid said: ﴿And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour﴾, i.e., a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of 'Isa, son of Mary, before the Day of Resurrection. Thus it has been reported from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The hadiths have been transmitted with mass narration (mutawatir) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he informed of the descent of 'Isa [son of Mary] [[Addition from T, M.]], peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just imam and a fair judge.

Allah, the Exalted, says: "Do these polytheists, who deny the messengers, await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?" That is, it is certainly going to happen without doubt and it will occur. These people are heedless of it and are not prepared for it [[addition from A.]]. When it comes, it will come upon them while they have no awareness of it, and then they will regret with the utmost regret, a regret that will neither benefit them nor ward off anything from them.

* *
