Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 43, verse 74–80:

When [Allah, exalted is He] mentioned the state of the blessed (al-su'ada'), He followed it with mention of the wretched (al-ashqiya'), saying: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, abiding eternally. It will not be lightened for them﴾, meaning for even an instant, ﴿and they will be in it in despair﴾, meaning hopeless of any good. ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: by their evil deeds, after the proofs had been established against them and the messengers had been sent to them, so they denied and disobeyed. Thus they were recompensed with a fitting recompense, ﴿and your Lord does not wrong the servants﴾.

﴿And they will call, "O Malik"﴾, and he is the keeper of the Fire.

Al-Bukhari said: Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Safwan ibn Ya'la, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting on the pulpit: ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us"﴾.

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4819).] Meaning: let Him take our souls so that He relieves us of what we are in, for they, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It will not be decreed for them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ [Fatir: 36]. Meaning: there is no exit for you from it, and no escape for you from it.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on surah 43, verses 81–89:

Allah says: "Say," O Muhammad: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers" (﴿إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ﴾). That is: if this were supposed, I would worship Him on that basis, because I am one of His servants, obedient to everything He commands me. I have no arrogance or refusal regarding His worship. So if this were supposed to be the case, but it is impossible with respect to Allah, the Exalted. A conditional does not imply that the condition occurs, nor even that it is permissible, as Allah says: ﴿If Allah had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whom He willed from among what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [az-Zumar: 4]

[And] [[Addition from manuscripts T and M.]] Some of the exegetes said regarding His words ﴿then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ that it means "the first of the ones who are unwilling (ānifīn)." Among them is Sufyan al-Thawri. Al-Bukhari also reported it, saying: "It is said: ﴿the first of the worshippers﴾ means the first of the deniers (al-jāhidīn), from 'abida, ya'badu (to be unwilling/disdainful)."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) cited as evidence for this view what he narrated through Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b told me, from Abu Qusayt [[In T: "what he narrated with its chain."]], from Ba'aja ibn Zayd al-Juhani: that a woman from among them entered upon her husband, who was also a man from among them, and she gave birth to a child after six months. Her husband mentioned this to Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, so he ordered that she be stoned. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, came in to him and said: "Allah says in His Book: ﴿And his carrying and weaning is thirty months﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], and He says: ﴿and his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14]." So Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I did not 'abada (disdain)," and he sent for her to be returned. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: "'abada" means "istankafa" (he refused/disdained).

[And] [[Addition from manuscripts T and M.]] The poet said:

Whenever the one who loves wills, he cuts off his friend,
and he disdains him without any doubt, wronging him.

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (25/60).]

This view is open to scrutiny, because how does it fit with the conditional, so that its meaning would be: "If this is the case, then I refuse it"? This needs consideration. Unless it is said that "in" (in) is not a conditional particle but a negation, as Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son﴾, meaning: "The Most Merciful did not have a son, and I am the first of the witnesses (al-shāhidīn)."

Qatadah said: It is a phrase from the speech of the Arabs: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾, meaning: "If that had not been the case, then it would not be appropriate."

Abu Sakhr said: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ means: "Then I am the first to worship Him by affirming that He has no son, and the first to declare His oneness." Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

Mujahid said: ﴿then I am the first of the worshippers﴾ means: "the first who worshipped Him and affirmed His oneness, and who denied you."

Al-Bukhari said: ﴿then I am the first of the worshippers﴾ means "the first of the disdainful (al-ānifīn)." These are two dialects: a man may be ʿābid and ʿabid (both meaning worshipper/disdainful).

The first view is closer to being a conditional and its consequent, but that condition is impossible.

Al-Suddi said regarding His words ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾: "It means: if He had a son, I would be the first to worship Him, on the basis that He has a son. But He has no son." This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, who rejected the view of those who claimed that "in" is negating.

For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ That is: exalted, sanctified and far removed is the Creator of things from having a son, for He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, having no equal and no peer, and so He has no son.

* *

His words ﴿So leave them to wade in vanity and to play﴾ mean: in their ignorance and error, and to play in their worldly life, ﴿until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. That is: they will soon know what their final state, their outcome, and their condition will be on that Day.

* *

His words ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾ mean: He is the God of those in the heaven and the God of those in the earth, whom the people of both worship, and all of them are humbled before Him and abased in His presence. ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.﴾

This verse is like His words: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth; He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾ [al-An'am: 3]. That is: He is the One called "Allah" in the heavens and the earth.

﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾. That is: He is their Creator, their Owner, and the One who disposes of them, without any opposition or hindrance. So He is exalted above having a son. "Blessed" (tabāraka) means that He is established as free from defects and imperfections, because He is the Lord, the Most High, the Mighty, the Owner of things, in whose hand are the reins of affairs, undoing and establishing. ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, that is, none reveals it at its time but He. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, that is, He will recompense each person for their deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

Then Allah says: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him will not possess intercession﴾, that is, the idols and images ﴿intercession﴾, meaning they have no power to intercede for them. ﴿Except those who testify to the truth and they know﴾. This is an exception of disconnection (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but whoever testifies to the truth with insight and knowledge, his intercession will benefit him before Him, by His permission for him.

Then He said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?﴾ That is: if you asked these polytheists who worship others besides Allah, "Who created them?", they would say, "Allah." That is: they acknowledge that He is the Creator of all things, alone, with no partner in that. Yet with this, they worship others besides Him, who own nothing and have no power over anything. So they are in the extreme of ignorance, foolishness and feebleness of intellect. For this reason He said: ﴿Then how are they deluded?﴾

And His words: ﴿And [his] saying, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe"﴾. That is: Muhammad said: his saying, that is, he complained to his Lord about his complaint concerning his people who denied him, saying: "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe," as Allah informs in another verse: ﴿And the Messenger said, "O my Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ [al-Furqan: 30]. What we have said is the meaning of the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Mujahid and Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir interpreted it accordingly [[Tafsir al-Tabari (25/62).]].

Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah (i.e., Ibn Mas'ud) recited: "And the Messenger said, 'O my Lord.'"

Mujahid said regarding His words ﴿And his saying, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe"﴾: "Then Allah fulfilled the saying of Muhammad."

Qatadah said: It is the saying of your Prophet ﷺ complaining about his people to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

Then Ibn Jarir mentioned two readings regarding His words ﴿And his saying, "O my Lord"﴾. One of them is the accusative (al-naṣb), and it has two explanations: the first is that it is coordinated (maʿṭūf) with His words ﴿We hear their secret and their private talk﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 80]; the second is that a verb is supposed, and it says: "qīlahu" (and He said). The second reading is the genitive (al-khafḍ): "wa-qīlihi," coordinated with His words ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, its supposed sense being: "and the knowledge of his saying."

* *

His words ﴿So turn away from them﴾ mean: from the polytheists, ﴿and say, "Peace."﴾ That is: do not respond to them with the like of the bad speech with which they address you, but be gentle with them, and forgive them in deed and in word. ﴿But they will soon know.﴾ This is a threat from Him, Exalted, against them. For this reason He brought upon them His punishment, which cannot be repelled, and He exalted His religion and His word, and afterwards prescribed jihad and fighting, until people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and Islam spread in the East and the West.

End of the commentary on Surah az-Zukhruf.

and he disdains him without any doubt, wronging him.

This view is open to scrutiny, because how does it fit with the conditional, so that its meaning would be: "If this is the case, then I refuse it"? This needs consideration. * *

This view is open to scrutiny, because how does it fit with the conditional, so that its meaning would be: "If this is the case, then I refuse it"? This needs consideration. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah (i.e., Ibn Mas'ud) recited: "And the Messenger said, 'O my Lord.'"

Qatadah said: It is the saying of your Prophet ﷺ complaining about his people to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

Then Ibn Jarir mentioned two readings regarding His words ﴿And his saying, "O my Lord"﴾. One of them is the accusative (al-naṣb), and it has two explanations: the first is that it is coordinated (maʿṭūf) with His words ﴿We hear their secret and their private talk﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 80]; the second is that a verb is supposed, and it says: "qīlahu" (and He said). The second reading is the genitive (al-khafḍ): "wa-qīlihi," coordinated with His words ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, its supposed sense being: "and the knowledge of his saying."

* *

His words ﴿So turn away from them﴾ mean: from the polytheists, ﴿and say, "Peace."﴾ That is: do not respond to them with the like of the bad speech with which they address you, but be gentle with them, and forgive them in deed and in word. ﴿But they will soon know.﴾ This is a threat from Him, Exalted, against them. For this reason He brought upon them His punishment, which cannot be repelled, and He exalted His religion and His word, and afterwards prescribed jihad and fighting, until people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and Islam spread in the East and the West.

End of the commentary on Surah az-Zukhruf.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on surah 43, verses 81–89:

Allah says: "Say," O Muhammad: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers" (﴿إِنْ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ﴾). That is: if this were supposed, I would worship Him on that basis, because I am one of His servants, obedient to everything He commands me. I have no arrogance or refusal regarding His worship. So if this were supposed to be the case, but it is impossible with respect to Allah, the Exalted. A conditional does not imply that the condition occurs, nor even that it is permissible, as Allah says: ﴿If Allah had wished to take a son, He would have chosen whom He willed from among what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [az-Zumar: 4]

[And] [[Addition from manuscripts T and M.]] Some of the exegetes said regarding His words ﴿then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ that it means "the first of the ones who are unwilling (ānifīn)." Among them is Sufyan al-Thawri. Al-Bukhari also reported it, saying: "It is said: ﴿the first of the worshippers﴾ means the first of the deniers (al-jāhidīn), from 'abida, ya'badu (to be unwilling/disdainful)."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) cited as evidence for this view what he narrated through Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b told me, from Abu Qusayt [[In T: "what he narrated with its chain."]], from Ba'aja ibn Zayd al-Juhani: that a woman from among them entered upon her husband, who was also a man from among them, and she gave birth to a child after six months. Her husband mentioned this to Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, so he ordered that she be stoned. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, came in to him and said: "Allah says in His Book: ﴿And his carrying and weaning is thirty months﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], and He says: ﴿and his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14]." So Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I did not 'abada (disdain)," and he sent for her to be returned. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: "'abada" means "istankafa" (he refused/disdained).

[And] [[Addition from manuscripts T and M.]] The poet said:

Whenever the one who loves wills, he cuts off his friend,
and he disdains him without any doubt, wronging him.

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (25/60).]

This view is open to scrutiny, because how does it fit with the conditional, so that its meaning would be: "If this is the case, then I refuse it"? This needs consideration. Unless it is said that "in" (in) is not a conditional particle but a negation, as Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son﴾, meaning: "The Most Merciful did not have a son, and I am the first of the witnesses (al-shāhidīn)."

Qatadah said: It is a phrase from the speech of the Arabs: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾, meaning: "If that had not been the case, then it would not be appropriate."

Abu Sakhr said: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ means: "Then I am the first to worship Him by affirming that He has no son, and the first to declare His oneness." Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

Mujahid said: ﴿then I am the first of the worshippers﴾ means: "the first who worshipped Him and affirmed His oneness, and who denied you."

Al-Bukhari said: ﴿then I am the first of the worshippers﴾ means "the first of the disdainful (al-ānifīn)." These are two dialects: a man may be ʿābid and ʿabid (both meaning worshipper/disdainful).

The first view is closer to being a conditional and its consequent, but that condition is impossible.

Al-Suddi said regarding His words ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾: "It means: if He had a son, I would be the first to worship Him, on the basis that He has a son. But He has no son." This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, who rejected the view of those who claimed that "in" is negating.

For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ That is: exalted, sanctified and far removed is the Creator of things from having a son, for He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, having no equal and no peer, and so He has no son.

* *

His words ﴿So leave them to wade in vanity and to play﴾ mean: in their ignorance and error, and to play in their worldly life, ﴿until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. That is: they will soon know what their final state, their outcome, and their condition will be on that Day.

* *

His words ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God in the earth﴾ mean: He is the God of those in the heaven and the God of those in the earth, whom the people of both worship, and all of them are humbled before Him and abased in His presence. ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.﴾

This verse is like His words: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth; He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾ [al-An'am: 3]. That is: He is the One called "Allah" in the heavens and the earth.

﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾. That is: He is their Creator, their Owner, and the One who disposes of them, without any opposition or hindrance. So He is exalted above having a son. "Blessed" (tabāraka) means that He is established as free from defects and imperfections, because He is the Lord, the Most High, the Mighty, the Owner of things, in whose hand are the reins of affairs, undoing and establishing. ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, that is, none reveals it at its time but He. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾, that is, He will recompense each person for their deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

Then Allah says: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him will not possess intercession﴾, that is, the idols and images ﴿intercession﴾, meaning they have no power to intercede for them. ﴿Except those who testify to the truth and they know﴾. This is an exception of disconnection (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but whoever testifies to the truth with insight and knowledge, his intercession will benefit him before Him, by His permission for him.

Then He said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah." Then how are they deluded?﴾ That is: if you asked these polytheists who worship others besides Allah, "Who created them?", they would say, "Allah." That is: they acknowledge that He is the Creator of all things, alone, with no partner in that. Yet with this, they worship others besides Him, who own nothing and have no power over anything. So they are in the extreme of ignorance, foolishness and feebleness of intellect. For this reason He said: ﴿Then how are they deluded?﴾

And His words: ﴿And [his] saying, "O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe"﴾.
